$$"] ["question-e39062c0-8f9b-52cc-adaa-1df745d5f896" :question/worked-solution "The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $1$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and the $4$th columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=1+1+2=4.
$$"] ["question-e39062c0-8f9b-52cc-adaa-1df745d5f896" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-a4adc5e4-eeb4-5d02-8d02-ca9f53944067" :answer-field/id #uuid
